title: Answer to Question: The Reality of Erdogan's Position and the Restoration of Relations with Armenia
text:
Answer to Question: The Reality of Erdogan's Position and the Restoration of Relations with Armenia

Question:

Erdogan repeatedly declared that he would not sign an agreement with Armenia to open the border and establish diplomatic relations with it... except after Armenia withdrew its army from the occupied lands of Azerbaijan in "Karabakh". But Erdogan's government signed an agreement on this matter on 10/10/2009 without the condition of Armenian withdrawal. And although the signing has taken place, Erdogan declared on 11/10/2009: "If Armenia does not withdraw from the occupied lands of Azerbaijan, Turkey will not take a positive position." And he added: "This withdrawal will also make it easier for the Turkish parliament to adopt the agreements (signed between Turkey and Armenia)" (Reuters, AFP, 11/10/2009). The question is:

What made Erdogan change his opinion? Furthermore, the signing has officially taken place, so what is the meaning of Erdogan's latest statement? Does it mean that if Armenia does not withdraw its army, he will cancel the agreement?

Answer:

This agreement was not born of its day; rather, it passed through several steps under American sponsorship from beginning to end, until it was signed on 11/10/2009. We will mention some of the notable steps, then explain the reason for the change in Erdogan's opinion and the meaning of his latest statement:

1- Obama, during his visit to Turkey on 6/4/2009, called for resolving the dispute between Turkey and Armenia and establishing peace between them. He met with their foreign ministers in the presence of the Swiss foreign minister, who sponsors the talks between the two parties. And the drawing up of a road map to achieve this was announced. The Turkish newspaper Sabah published on 24/4/2009 the road map that America had drawn up, which included clauses, among them Armenia's recognition of the current border drawn between Turkey and Armenia on 13/10/1921 in the Treaty of Kars, signed between the Ottoman State and the Soviet Union and endorsed in the Treaty of Lausanne, that is, the endorsement of the current border between Turkey and Armenia. Among the clauses of the American road map is the establishment of a commission to re-examine the so-called genocide of the Armenians, another clause relating to opening the border and trade exchange between them, and another clause relating to restoring diplomatic relations and the exchange of ambassadors between them.

2- Several months earlier, talks had taken place with Swiss mediation between the foreign ministers of the two countries, and they reached an agreement on 22/4/2009 on a comprehensive framework for normalising relations between their two countries that satisfies both parties. The talks continued until they reached on 1/9/2009 a concurrence of views to sign a comprehensive agreement between them.

3- On 10/10/2009 the signing of the comprehensive agreement was announced according to the road map that America had drawn up earlier. The Turkish foreign minister Ahmet Davutoglu signed with the Armenian foreign minister Edward Nalbandian, with Swiss mediation, in Zurich, under the supervision and execution of the US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, who played the effective role in this signing. The signing was attended by the two other parties of the Minsk Group: Russia, represented by its foreign minister Lavrov, and France, represented by its foreign minister Kouchner, in addition to the European Union's foreign policy representative Solana and the foreign minister of Slovakia, as witnesses to the agreement, which was described as the historic agreement to end the Turkish-Armenian conflict. International and Turkish news agencies published the text of the full protocol signed by the foreign ministers of Turkey and Armenia, and it includes: (recognition of the current border and the opening of this border between them within two months; establishment of diplomatic relations and exchange of ambassadors; opening mutual consulates to assist and protect the citizens of the two countries according to the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations signed in 1963; and development of bilateral relations in all fields: political, economic, energy, transport and communications, and in the scientific and technical fields, culture, environment, tourism and other things. And they work together on regional and international cooperation in the United Nations, the European Union and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, and work together to achieve regional and international security and stability, the development of democracy in the region, combating cross-border organised crime, and combating terrorism and the smuggling of weapons and drugs, and working to resolve regional and international conflicts by peaceful means according to international rules and laws, establishing regular consultations between them, and establishing and developing dialogue for impartial scientific examination of the historical documents and sources relating to their two peoples with the aim of establishing mutual trust between the two peoples...). In the matter of scientific examination, it refers to the events of 1915 CE, which Armenia used to call genocide, although Obama, paving the way for this agreement, called it by another name in his speech delivered on 24/4/2009 on the occasion of the anniversary of the so-called genocide of the Armenians, where he expressed it as a terrible calamity and not as genocide or ethnic cleansing, and that was, as we said, paving the way for this agreement.

4- This agreement covered all fields and resolved all the problems between the two countries, but it did not touch with a single letter upon the problem of Armenia's occupation of the lands of Azerbaijan in "Karabakh" and around it, nor did it touch upon the problem of the Azeris displaced from these lands, bearing in mind that Turkey cut its relations with Armenia and closed the border with it in 1993 in protest against Armenia's occupation of the Nagorno-Karabakh region together with seven districts, which represent between 20% and 24% of the area of Azerbaijan, and from which about one million Azeris were displaced... But Turkey has now abandoned all of that, which angered Azerbaijan and left it an easy morsel in the hands of the major states represented by the Minsk Group of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, represented by America, Russia and France, which has been working since the cessation of the war between Azerbaijan and Armenia in 1993 ("which had begun at the end of 1987") to find a solution to the Azeri-Armenian problem.

5- Russia intervened on the side of the Armenians and helped them during Armenia's aggression against Azerbaijan, but the rulers of Turkey and Iran, the two Muslim countries, did not intervene to support Azerbaijan, the Muslim country neighbouring Iran and counted as close to Turkey! Were it not for the Russian intervention on the side of the Armenians, and Iran's failure to support its neighbour Azerbaijan — indeed it did not cut its relations with Armenia nor close the border — and likewise the failure of Turkey to intervene militarily and its not supplying Azerbaijan with any military aid to repel the Armenian aggressors and the Russians behind them, were it not for that, the Armenians would not have been able to triumph over the Azeris, who resisted the Armenians and the Russians alone for a period of more than five years.

Thus the rulers of Turkey and Iran forsook the Muslim country Azerbaijan during the war, so Armenia, with the help of the Russians, was able to occupy Azeri lands.

6- The rulers of Turkey were not content with forsaking Azerbaijan during the war; rather, today they are likewise forsaking it by signing this agreement before the Azeri lands have returned to their owners and their displaced people have returned to them. So the Azeri reaction was angry at Turkey, and it considered this to be against its interests. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan issued a statement in which it said: "The normalisation of relations between Turkey and Armenia before the withdrawal of the Armenian forces from the occupied Azeri region directly contradicts the interests of Azerbaijan, and casts its shadow over the brotherly relations between Azerbaijan and Turkey, which are built on deep roots." The statement added: "Azerbaijan sees that the opening of the border threatens peace and stability in the region." And the Azeri Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in its statement: "Baku expects Ankara to abide by the promises made by Turkish officials not to open the border except when the Armenian forces withdraw from the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region." The statement said: "Azerbaijan's position on this matter is unambiguous" (AFP and Iran's Al-Alam, 11/10/2009).

7- As for the reasons that led Erdogan to change his opinion and his government to sign this agreement with Armenia in Zurich, they are the American orders, because of the great service that this agreement performs for America. For by this agreement it intends to win Armenia and Azerbaijan to its side and to distance Russian influence from them, so that the circle of America's influence in the South Caucasus expands:

As for Armenia: after America took Georgia, which borders Armenia from the north, from Russian influence through a colour revolution, it looked towards Armenia to weaken Russian influence in its old and traditional region. The signing of this Turkish-Armenian agreement is a great opportunity for America to take Armenia from Russia and place it under its control, and a victory for America over Russia, and this will be reinforced directly through Turkey. This appeared from the statement of the US Secretary of State as she was leaving Zurich, flying with joy, when she declared that: "her country will work with all its capabilities to make the protocol signed between Turkey and Armenia succeed" (Anadolu Agency, 11/10/2009). Therefore the Americans will put all their weight behind getting the Turkish parliament to sign this agreement, and their man Erdogan will work for that with all his methods and his deception to make the members of his party in parliament sign this agreement. It appears that matters are moving towards the signing of that agreement, as no serious opposition has appeared from the Republican People's Party in Turkey, whose members consider themselves brothers of the Armenians and not enemies. So with the votes of these two parties the agreement will be ratified in the Turkish parliament. And on the Armenian side there is also no serious opposition; for months matters have been prepared for it there, and it was not linked to the withdrawal of the Armenians from the occupied Azeri lands, so its ratification there will also be easy...

As for Azerbaijan: it wavers in its relations between Russia and America, as it goes along with both states in opening the door to them for investment in the field of oil and gas. Therefore it accepted the extension of the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline to pour into the Mediterranean Sea, and allowed American companies to invest in the field of oil, foremost among them the Chevron company, alongside the Russian companies. It also allows Russia to establish military bases on its territory: Russia has the Gabala base in Azerbaijan, in which powerful radars are installed, and the base has been used by the Russians since 1984, and the agreement for its use by the Russians was renewed in 2002 for another ten years, and this shows the extent of Russian influence in Azerbaijan. So Azerbaijan's connection with Russia is still strong. Nevertheless, Russia previously offered America to deploy its radars alongside Russia's radars in its "Gabala" base in return for America abandoning the placing of its radars in the Czech Republic and the installation of missiles in Poland, and Azerbaijan did not object to that proposal... That is, Azerbaijan tries to satisfy Russia and America. However, America wants its influence to be effectively present in Azerbaijan, and it saw in the Turkish-Armenian agreement a strong means of pressure on Azerbaijan to accept American influence completely, and then America would intervene to resolve the Armenian-Azeri problem away from Russia.

And although the agreement constituted a strong blow to Azerbaijan, which controls the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline and can close it as a reaction, America relies on Turkey to tame Azerbaijan. Azerbaijan cannot adopt a state of hostility with Turkey and dare to close the pipeline, or take wayward reactions such as harassing the American companies investing in the field of oil and gas... That is, America is reassured by the misleading and cunning conduct that Erdogan carries out with Azerbaijan, making America's interests his scale of values, caring neither about the occupied lands of Azerbaijan nor about its displaced people. Had he cared about that, he would have risen and helped Azerbaijan at that time and supplied it with military force, and he himself would have contributed militarily to returning the occupied lands to Azerbaijan, and his government would not have signed this latest agreement in which it forsook the Azeri brothers, as they always boasted by saying "the brotherly relationship between Turkey and Azerbaijan has deep roots"!

8- As for Erdogan's statement on 11/10/2009, the day after the signing of the agreement, in which he said: "If Armenia does not withdraw from the occupied lands of Azerbaijan, Turkey will not take a positive position," and he said: "We want the problem of Nagorno-Karabakh and the occupied regions to be resolved in the same way, and if the problems between Azerbaijan and Armenia are resolved, then it will be easier for Turkish society to support the normalisation of relations between Turkey and Armenia. And it will also make it easier for the Turkish parliament to adopt the agreements (signed between Turkey and Armenia)" (Reuters, AFP, 11/10/2009), it is an outright lie, a form of charlatanry and misleading. Would any rational person believe that Erdogan's government signs all these agreements with the Armenians under American sponsorship and with international attendance, and then after that Erdogan declares that Turkey will not take a positive position towards the agreement and that normalisation will not be easy? This is nothing but to deceive public opinion in Turkey and an attempt to deceive the Azeris, who have realised his false promises!

This statement and its like are a twisting of words and a playing with them that will not hold out for long!
